recipes.name: Fresh Pear Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Place a rimmed baking sheet on the lower oven rack to preheat.
Line the bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate with one pie crust. Set second crust aside.
Combine sugar, flour, cinnamon, lemon zest, and salt in a mixing bowl.
Arrange pear slices in layers in prepared crust, sprinkling sugar mixture over each layer. Dot with butter and sprinkle with lemon juice.

Moisten the rim of bottom crust with water, then cover filling with remaining pie crust. Trim excess pastry, press the edges together to seal, and flute as desired. Cut several slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.

Carefully place the pie on the hot baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven on the baking sheet for 10 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C); bake until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbly, 35 to 40 minutes longer. Transfer the pie to a wire rack to cool before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Pear Pie
raw_recipe.description: This easy pear pie is made with freshly sliced pears tossed with cinnamon sugar and baked in a double-crust pie shell for a fabulous fall dessert.

review.reviewBody: The filling is yummy - the only thing I did was to mix the sugar mixture together with the pears as others have suggested. But since I am not a baker and the thought of making the top crust look nice was terrifying, I made a crumble topping: 1/2 cup each butter and brown sugar mixed together with 1 cup flour. Pour the crumbles over the pears and bake at 350 for about an hour. I took it to a party tonight and everyone raved, even hubby who claims to not like pears. Thanks!!

My family has been making pear pies for generations so I consider myself somewhat of an expert on the subject. The reason your pear pies are tasting like apple pies is the CINNAMON!!! Do what our family does and use NUTMEG! Other reviewers are correct: make sure your pears are ripe almost to the point of being soft. Also, don't be afraid of using salt in your dessert recipes! This recipe says use 1/4 teaspoon salt. That's not enough to even bother with! I would at least double that, and the reason is: SALT MAKES SUGAR TASTE EVEN SWEETER! We also traditionally sprinkle some white sugar over the top crust before baking. This always helps us differentiate it from an apple pie at a family meal.

I have made this pie at least 10 times now, since we are hooked on it. Originally came upon recipe because we have a pear tree that gave us an over abundance, more than we could give away or store. The first time I made the recipe I followed exactly as written, until I came to the lemon zest and realized I didn't have a whole lemon. I did have fresh ginger and grated some of that in. My pie was wonderful! Since then I've made a few variations of this original recipe and my winning one is, I use the lemon zest AND fresh grated ginger - at least a good heaping tablespoon. And I have changed the 3 tablespoons of flour to 4 tablespoons of corn starch, and changed the 1/2 cup of white sugar to 1/4 cup Splenda and 1/4 cup brown sugar!. Wonderful - the ginger gives it a taste that is not over powering where anyone can put their finger on what it is - but it makes it most unique. The corn starch allows the cutting of the pie to come out picture perfect

Probably the best pie I have ever made... I did read previous reviews and tweaked it a little. I used 1/4 cup each brown sugar and white sugar. Instead of lemon zest, I subbed 1 tablespoon of grated ginger root, 1 tsp. lemon juice, 3/4 tsp. of nutmeg and only 1/4 tsp. of cinnamon. Combine all the ingredients together and mixed thoroughly before putting into the pie shell. I did not use any more lemon juice to sprinkle over the pie, but dotted with 2 tsp, of butter before baking.
With a glass dish, the pie took much longer to bake; probably 20-25 minutes more. Next time I will increase temperature to 375.
Honestly the most delicious pie I have made in my 40 years of baking pies. Thank you for sharing, a true winner!

This was good, but required a number of changes for me. I use the Emile Henri pie dishes, so this took 7.5 C of sliced pears, added 1/4 C brown sugar, reduced cinnamon to 1/2 t., then added 1/4 t. each of powdered ginger, allspice, cardamom and fresh grated nutmeg. Heavy on the lemon zest, tossed the lemon juice in with pears as I sliced them, used 4 T cornstarch and 1 T flour, mixed sugar and spice in with that and incorporated it into pears before turning into crust laden pie dish. Topped the top crust with brushing of melted butter and sprinkled white sugar. Took approx an hour to bake and bubble. It still could have taken heavier hand of spices and zest and sugars for that many pears, but it was a nice subtle flavor which allowed the complexity of the four varieties of pears I used to shine. This amt of cornstarch and flour was perfect for a great set with no runny juices for that amt of pears, it cut beautifully. Will make again for something different.

This was really tasty and easy to make. I did make some minor changes based on advice of past reviewers though. I just tossed the sliced pears with the sugar mixture rather than layering as directed (I then just placed the mixture in the pie crust about a third at a time, dotting with butter and drizzling lemon juice on top after each addition). I used 6 cups of pears and added about 1/4 tsp of nutmeg. I also used a crumb topping rather than a top crust (1/4 cup butter, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 3/4 cup flour- thanks to a previous reviewer's suggestion) because that is my preference for pies. A really nice pie- I loved the addition of lemon!

Upon the recommendation of a friend of mine, are used Kinnickinnic Gf tart shells, skipped the butter, used coconut sugar in place of white sugar, tapioca starch in place of the flower, and combined all the filling ingredients together. They turned out excellent, I would skip the lemon zest next time as it is very much at the front of the flavour-fine for me, but not so loved by my family.

Very good and simple pie. It does taste like apple if you use cinnamon so I added a little nutmeg which brought out the pear flavor nicely. I used unripe Bartlett pears (I was in a rush) but an extra 20 minutes in the oven while covered with foil softened them up nicely. Also, they didn’t turn into mush which I feel happens often with fruit pies.

Love this as a base recipe, I swapped the white sugar for light brown, added 1 tsp of vanilla, 1/2 tsp ginger, 1/2 tsp nutmeg and just mixed everything together except the butter that I diced up and scattered on top of the filling before covering. It was yum yum! I used Pillsbury Refrigerated Pie Crusts and just brushed the top with butter then cinnamon/sugar worked well.

The filling of this pear pie is absolutely delicious! The little hint of lemon zest and juice really accentuates the pears and brings out their flavor. I felt the amount of cinnamon was spot on! The pears did juice out a lot, which sogged out the storebought pie crust. I would definitely go with a homemade next time--they tend to be a bit 'heartier' in holding up to fruit juices, and they taste better too. I would probably also use corn starch in place of flour in the filling, and maybe add just a touch more of it. My pie also needed to bake for 60 minutes after reducing the heat. It was not even close to done at the 35-40 minute mark. It was still a great pear pie, though; and one that I would make again. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

This was probably the best fruit pie I've made. I tweaked the recipe by using coconut palm sugar (a brown sugar) instead of white, using nutmeg instead of cinnamon, and using orange zest/ juice instead of lemon. I also doubled the salt. I did a lattice crust (with store bought pie dough) and sprinkled more of the coconut palm sugar on top. 

It was delicious, definitely didn't taste like apple pie, and was amazing warmed up with vanilla ice cream on top.
Loved it! Don’t change a thing. This was a good way to use up Bartlett pears. Everyone raved over it.

Changes were using half brown sugar and half white, 4 tablespoons of corn starch (instead of flour), 1/4 teaspoon of allspice, less lemon zest, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, 10 pears total, mixing the pears with the sugar mix, topping the top crust with melted butter and vanilla bean sugar, and cooking at 350F for just 25 minutes (in a toaster oven). Next time though I would do only white sugar, flour (no corn starch), no lemon zest or juice, no allspice, and simply sprinkling the sugar mix per the recipe.

Easy to make and has a delicious flavor. I did add 3/4 cup of brown sugar instead of the white sugar and had a little over 5 cups of cut up pears. The suggested thickener of flour was not enough & pie was too runny for my liking so I will add cornstarch instead of flour next time.
Need a dessert cookbook for dummies? This recipe was simple and very easy to make and it came out perfectly. Taste wonderful. This is a must try.

Local box store had a big bag of organic pears that ripened faster than I could eat them. I mixed the peeled and sliced pears with brown sugar, flour, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl and added to my pie crust already coated.It turned out delicous. One guest later told me they did not like pears but thought they were eating an apple pie and loved it!
Easy to make. Added dried mango to help with excess liquid.
